Hi all,

Quick technical responses to Alice's questions — high-level, non-normative (we can schedule a security-architecture review with our InfoSec SME if needed):

1) Region pinning granularity:
- Redwood supports per-customer and per-route region pinning. You can configure a policy that routes EU-labeled customer traffic to EU-only endpoints. For extra isolation, Private deployment (VPC) allows you to restrict egress completely.
- For hosted customers, we offer region pinning with an SLA-backed constraint: requests that are eligible for EU routing will be served from EU regions.

2) Cross-region failover and backups:
- Failover triggers: health checks at the region and availability-zone level; automatic failover occurs when the primary region is unavailable for a configurable period. Failover is policy-driven — you can choose allowed failover targets (e.g., EU-only) or allow global failover.
- Backups/replication: Backups of persistent config/metadata are stored per-region by default. For model artifacts and cold backups, replication policy is configurable; we can restrict replication to EU regions only. Snapshot/backup retention schedules are configurable via the console or API.

3) Data retention, logging & PII handling:
- Input/output logging: By default, we retain request metadata and short-term logs to support observability. Model inputs/outputs are not persisted to long-term storage unless you enable enhanced logging (required for some eval features).
- Route-level logging controls: You can disable or redact model input/outputs per-route. Retention windows are configurable (30/90/365 days) and you can set zero retention for specific routes.
- Audit logs & access: Audit logs and admin access traces are stored in the pinned region. Role-based access controls integrate with your SSO/KMS for access.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a region architecture diagram and a short SOC2 summary to the shared MAP.

I'll follow up with a suggested configuration snippet and a sample failover policy for Acme — looping Marissa to help draft the mutual action plan and procurement checklist.
